title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with tomatoes and dark‑green vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: A dish made from eggs, prepared as an omelet or scrambled eggs, with fresh tomatoes and dark‑green vegetables (spinach, broccoli, kale). Eggs provide high‑quality protein, while the vegetables add vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most affordable and nutrient‑dense foods used worldwide.
Dark‑green vegetables are rich in chlorophyll, giving them their characteristic color and boosting antioxidant properties.
Tomatoes contain lycopene, which becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
An omelet can be prepared quickly, and adding vegetables makes the meal more filling and nutritious.
Different cultures have their own omelet styles: France adds herbs, Japan uses soy sauce, the US often includes cheese and bacon.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs supply all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs are rich in B12, riboflavin, and biotin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Dark‑green vegetables and tomatoes provide vitamins C, E, carotenoids, and lycopene that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The added vegetables contribute fiber, aiding digestion and promoting satiety.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish contains iron, magnesium, potassium, and phosphorus, essential for normal body functions.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol levels should moderate yolk intake.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked eggs can harbor Salmonella; ensure eggs are cooked through.

items.title: Oxalates in green vegetables
items.content: Certain dark‑green vegetables (e.g., spinach) are high in oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat eggs with a splash of milk or water, season with salt and pepper. In a lightly oiled pan, sauté diced tomatoes and green vegetables until tender, then pour in the egg mixture and cook to the desired consistency, gently lifting the edges as it sets.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Consume the omelet soon after cooking. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Keep raw eggs refrigerated at 1‑4 °C in their original carton.
